title: SYSK’s Summer Movie Playlist: What's the deal with Bond, James Bond?
summary: Summer Movie Playlist rerun of SYSK's July 2010 episode "What's the Deal with Bond? James Bond?" Hosts Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant cover Ian Fleming and his WWII intelligence work, the James Bond novels and their publication order, the Thunderball rights litigation, the character's backstory and Scottish/Swiss parents, double-O status, Q, M, Moneypenny and other recurring characters, the villains, the actors who played Bond (Barry Nelson, Sean Connery, George Lazenby, Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton, Pierce Brosnan, Daniel Craig), the unofficial Never Say Never Again, the code name theory, Bond girls, theme songs, box office, and a listener email about samurai Miyamoto Musashi.
rerun_of: What's the Deal with Bond? James Bond?

segments.title: Welcome to the Summer Movie Playlist
segments.summary: Josh introduces the summer movie playlist and the 2010 Bond episode being rebroadcast; hosts open with banter about James Bond as a blunt instrument and his gadgets and technology.

segments.title: Ian Fleming's wartime intelligence career
segments.summary: Hosts discuss Ian Fleming's background as a journalist and stockbroker, his Royal Navy service, and his intelligence work in Washington, DC, including photographing documents. They mention William Stevenson (Intrepid) as an inspiration for Bond and Roald Dahl as a fellow spy-ring member.

segments.title: Fleming's life and the Bond novels
segments.summary: Fleming's playboy lifestyle, skiing and diving, and his Jamaica estate GoldenEye, where he wrote a book each year. They discuss the name James Bond as deliberately boring, the count of Bond novels and short story collections, and that the films were released out of novel order. The Thunderball rights dispute led to Doctor No being filmed first.

segments.title: James Bond's character and background
segments.summary: Bond's Scottish father and Swiss mother were added after Sean Connery was cast, according to the hosts. Bond's birth date varies across accounts. Bond joins MI6 after WWII, earns double-O status by killing two people, and the hosts note the number seven agent origin. They then move to Bond's traits: fashion, cars, martinis, martial arts, and the Walther PPK.

segments.title: Bond villains
segments.summary: Hosts discuss villains including Doctor No, Goldfinger, Oddjob, Jaws, Blofeld and SPECTRE, Max Zorin played by Christopher Walken, and Tanya Roberts' Bond girl role. They discuss the quality of recent villains.

segments.title: Double-O Six, Timothy Dalton and Pierce Brosnan
segments.summary: Hosts discuss Alec Trevelyan, Pierce Brosnan's Remington Steele run, and Timothy Dalton being offered the role early on. They debate Brosnan's films and the darker direction of the franchise after Roger Moore.

segments.title: M, Q, Felix Leiter, and Moneypenny
segments.summary: The hosts cover M and the MI6 leadership including Judi Dench, Q and his branch, R, Felix Leiter actors, the CIA/DEA American counterpart Jack Wade, and Moneypenny.

segments.title: Bond on television and the actors who played him
segments.summary: Barry Nelson played Bond in a 1954 CBS TV adaptation of Casino Royale in Climax!, the first actor to play Bond. The hosts discuss George Lazenby's Australian background and short career, and then list the official films, the 1983 unofficial Never Say Never Again, and the actor sequence.

segments.title: Bond actors debate and the code name theory
segments.summary: Hosts discuss Timothy Dalton's films and the Roger Moore era. They then describe the code name theory that each actor played a different man using the name James Bond, its supporting evidence, and holes in the theory. They recommend fan sites.

segments.title: Roger Moore, Bond trivia and Albert Broccoli
segments.summary: Chuck defends several Roger Moore films. Josh shares a trivia item that producer Albert Broccoli's family invented broccoli. Hosts discuss MGM's financial trouble delaying the next film.

segments.title: Bond girls, theme songs, and box office
segments.summary: Hosts discuss favorite Bond girls including Carrie Lowell, Ursula Andress, and names like Honey Ryder and Pussy Galore. They discuss theme songs by Shirley Bassey, Carly Simon, Nancy Sinatra, Tom Jones, Garbage, Sheryl Crow, Madonna, and Jack White with Alicia Keys. They discuss the title sequences, then the adjusted box office of Thunderball, Goldfinger, and Casino Royale, and the Bond cars.

segments.title: Inspector Gadget comparison and closing remarks
segments.summary: Josh says Inspector Gadget resembles James Bond. He points listeners to the website and the search bar, then introduces listener mail.

segments.title: Listener mail: samurai and Miyamoto Musashi
segments.summary: A listener named Thomas writes that the podcast should have covered Miyamoto Musashi, describes his Book of Five Rings and combat record, and notes wooden bokken used as weapons and his two-sword fighting.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh asks for listener contributions on James Bond and gives the contact address. Chuck closes with the HowStuffWorks website reference.
